trigger_record.summary: Calibration drift in the mid-risk band: predicted default rates diverged from realised rates over eight consecutive weeks.

delta_description.summary: Expected-to-actual default ratio moved from 1.02 to 1.19 in deciles 4 to 6. No model version change in the period; the shift tracks a change in applicant mix following a new broker channel.

reliability_impact_analysis.assessment: Mid-band applicants are being under-priced for risk. Exposure is bounded because the affected deciles represent 14 percent of approvals and manual underwriter review already applies above the referral threshold. Left uncorrected, the drift would compound as the broker channel grows.
reliability_impact_analysis.root_cause: Applicant mix shift from the new broker channel introduced a segment under-represented in the training window, degrading calibration without materially affecting rank-order discrimination.

drift_indicators: population stability index 0.18 on applicant income band
broker channel share up from 3 percent to 11 percent of volume
monitoring_snapshot.notes: Discrimination remains within tolerance; the failure is calibration, not ranking.

decision_record.rationale: Rank-ordering still holds, so the scorecard retains value, but pricing on the affected deciles is no longer defensible. Narrow automated approval to deciles 1 to 3 and route deciles 4 to 6 to underwriter review until a recalibration is validated.
temporary_controls: Automated approval suspended for deciles 4 to 6
Underwriter review mandatory for the affected bands
Weekly calibration reporting to the model risk forum
